applies_why: The judge resolves a pressed chain issue by checking whether a verse names whose body is the channel, rather than by weighing the pressed chains by footing.
quote: the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase 'by footing, never verse by verse' — I weighed (1) comparing the whole pressed chains by footing against (2) resolving the point because no verse expressly names the channel.
why: Because it treats the lack of an express verse naming the channel as leaving the point open, it uses the retired stating-verse test rather than chain-against-chain footing.
